title: Program Manager Electronics / STW
description:
Together We Saves Lives by Innovation!

The keys to success are yours at Joyson Safety Systems!  We are a global leader in design, development and manufacturing of safety-critical systems and components for automotive and non-automotive markets.  We are dedicated to delivering life-saving technology to customers worldwide. Joyson Safety Systems harnesses collaboration and innovation to ensure quality and exemplary service for our customers worldwide.  Our company is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, USA, with a global network of more than 30,000 employees in 22 countries.

Position Summary

The Program Manager is responsible for leading the development and launch of automotive steering wheel electronics programs from award through production. This role serves as the primary customer interface and is accountable for achieving program objectives related to timing, quality, cost, profitability, and customer satisfaction. The Program Manager works closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and Sales teams to ensure successful program execution.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead steering wheel electronics programs from development through launch and production.

• Serve as the primary customer contact for program-related activities.

• Manage program timing, budgets, deliverables, and profitability.

• Coordinate cross-functional teams to achieve quality, cost, and launch objectives.

• Drive issue resolution, risk management, and change management activities.

• Support APQP, PPAP, prototype builds, validation testing, and production launches.

• Communicate program status, risks, and recovery plans to customers and leadership.

• Collaborate with global engineering and manufacturing teams to ensure successful program execution.

Qualifications:

Required

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field.

• 5+ years of automotive program management, engineering, or product development experience.

• Experience with automotive electronics, steering wheel systems, controls, switches, sensors, HMI, or related products preferred.

• Knowledge of APQP, PPAP, product launches, and customer program management.

• Strong leadership, communication, project management, and organizational skills.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred Qualifications

• Tier 1 automotive supplier experience.

• Experience working directly with OEM customers.

• PMP certification or equivalent project management training.

Job Summary

The Analytical Chemist in the Armada Chemical Laboratory will perform quantitative analysis on chemical samples (raw materials and pyrotechnics) using advanced laboratory instruments. This role maintains strict quality control, troubleshoots instrumentation, and ensures compliance with ISO 17025.

Key Responsibilities

• Sample Analysis: Run tests on raw materials, in-process items, and finished products using techniques like high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), ion chromatography (IC), Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).

• Method Development & Validation: Develop, validate, and transfer analytical methods to support product testing and quality standards.

• Data Management & Reporting: Record experimental data accurately, interpret results, investigate out-of-specification results, and write technical reports.

• Equipment Maintenance: Calibrate, clean, and maintain complex lab instruments and handle troubleshooting.

• Regulatory Compliance: Adhere to safety protocols, company policies, and ISO 17025 guidelines during all laboratory operations.

• Inventory Control: Monitor and manage laboratory supplies, chemical reagents, and consumables.

• Quality Management System: Create and revise work instructions for various laboratory methods and procedures.

Preferred Qualifications

• Education: Bachelor's degree (B.S.) in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Analytical Chemistry, or a closely related field is preferred, but not manditory.

• Experience: Working experience in a laboratory setting and the handling of hazardous chemicals.

• Technical Skills:

• Proficiency in HPLC, IC, FTIR, and ICP-OES.

• Strong data management and interpretation ability.

• Understanding of statistics and data analysis.

• Knowledge of ISO 17025 laboratory requirements.

• Soft Skills: High attention to detail, strong problem-solving capabilities, and effective written and verbal communication.
